scope: One root-only diagnostic run on the existing private Linux/Kata host used byte-verified immutable v7 Jobs/worker source, the installed watchdog socket and the installed identity-service cgroup. Only a private test copy of the synthetic JSON fixture received a 20-second delay. Shields Up was observed false while the service was running and again at fault injection. The installed watchdog stopped the service after lease loss; the installed service lifecycle close hook then made Shields Up true. The test's emergency fallback did not run.
limits: The root driver supplied synthetic owner scope directly; OIDC/browser authorization and the unchanged production JSON action were not exercised by this fault check.

The observation verifies a false-to-true Shields Up transition after watchdog-induced service stop with no diagnostic fallback. It does not isolate every internal systemd timing step or establish a hard fail-close deadline.
One bounded resource-absence poll is not a 30-second SLA under arbitrary runtime stalls or host disconnects.
The installed socket messages were not independently packet-traced. The test exercised the pinned Jobs/worker code and installed socket.
